etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 取(と)り (tori, “taking”, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 取(と)る (toru, “to take”)) + 敢(あ)えず (aezu, from the negative form of 敢(あ)ふ (afu, “to bear, endure”)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/pa/ → /ɸa/ → /ha/
From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *pa.
Cognate with 歯 (ha, “tooth”). Possibly also related to 葉 (ha, “leaf”), but the pitch accents do not match. Compare English blade, which also meant “leaf”.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/jaki ɸa/ → /jakiba/ → /jaĩba/ → /jaiba/
イ音便(おんびん) (i-onbin) form of 焼き刃 (yakiba), a compound of 焼き (yaki, “burned, fired”) + 刃 (ha, “edge, blade”, see above). The ha changes to ba as an instance of rendaku (連濁).
Compare to つけやきば (tsukeyakiba), where the ki does not undergo the same euphonic change.
First attested in the Taiheiki of the late 1300s.

etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 富(と)む (tomu, “to be rich”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From 小(こ) (ko-, “little”) + 切(きっ)手(て) (kitte, “postage stamp”).
The kitte changes to gitte as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Derived via regular historical shifts from the classical lower bigrade (カ行下二段活用 (ka-gyō shimo nidan katsuyō)) verb 授(さづ)く (sazuku).
A surface analysis would suggest that this ultimately derives as a compound of さ (sa, of uncertain meaning) + 付ける (tsukeru, “to stick or attach something to something else; to put something somewhere”).
First attested in ideographic form in the Nihon Shoki of 720, and in phonetic spelling in the Man'yōshū of 759.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From 逸 (ichi-, “very”) + 著し (shirushi, “clear, obvious, conspicuous”, a ku-adjective).
Attested in the Heian period as a ku-adjective pronounced いちしるし (ichishirushi). Since the Muromachi period, it became pronounced いちじるし (ichijirushi), where the shirushi changes to jirushi as an instance of rendaku (連濁). Since around the Edo period, it changed conjugation class and became a shiku-adjective.
The modern form is from いちじるしき (ichijirushiki), the 連体形 (rentaikei, “attributive form”) of the Late Middle Japanese shiku-adjective いちじるし (ichijirushi), with the medial /-k-/ falling out.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 試(こころ)みる (kokoromiru, “to try, attempt”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from the older reading さいぎる, from the syncope of the /k/ in さきぎる (sakigiru), from 先 (saki, “in front”) + 切る (kiru, “cut”), literally “to cut off (from) the front”.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Old reading of the more modern さえぎる, originally from 先切(さきき)る (sakikiru)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 音(ね) (ne, “tone; sound”) + 色(いろ) (iro, “colour”). Compare German Klangfarbe (literally “sound-color”) and English tone color.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound verb from 飲(の)み (nomi, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 飲(の)む (nomu, “to drink; to swallow”)) + 込(こ)む (komu, “to go into”).
